headline: LLMs and retrieval pipelines convert literature into structured toxicology and biochemistry databases
label: Llm Assisted Literature Curation
summary: New toxicology tools and two NAR database updates use LLM extraction to build curated resources from literature, alongside a dated-evidence benchmark.
synthesis: The dominant thread is LLM-based extraction from the literature into structured, domain-specific resources. In toxicology, AOP-Smart-Finder combines LLMs and RAG in a human-AI hybrid framework for AOP evidence mapping, AOPTK offers open-source extraction of chemical-effect relationships, and a continuous pipeline mines PubMed/PMC full texts into a 189,212-finding hepatotoxicity knowledge base. Two database updates apply the same approach to protein data: ThermoMutDB 2.0 uses LLM-plus-rule semiautomated curation with mutant structural models, and BioLiP3 integrates curated affinities with LLM-enabled literature mining. What is new is the extension of LLM-assisted curation from toxicology into established structural-biology databases. The dated gene-evidence tables are adjacent: they support leakage-aware retrospective evaluation of gene prioritization and are not described as LLM-based.
